question: Which of the following is a risk with regard to the Green Revolution?

options.text: Increased disparities between small and big farmers
Increase in productivity in food grains

solution:
The correct answer is __**Increased disparities between small and big farmers.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The Green Revolution,** which **refers to the large-scale introduction of high-yielding varieties of seeds**, **fertilizers**, and **pesticides **in agriculture, has been criticized for its negative impact on small farmers.
 
• **Due to the high cost of these inputs**, **small farmers often find it difficult to adopt the new technologies** and compete with larger, wealthier farmers who can afford them.
 
• As a result, it has **led to increased disparities between small and big farmers**, with the latter reaping most of the benefits. This has led to a concentration of land and wealth in the hands of a few, while many small farmers have been pushed into debt and poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Green Revolution:**

 
• The **Green Revolution **was a major initiative that aimed to increase the production and quality of food crops, especially wheat and rice, in India, by introducing new technologies, such as high-yielding varieties of seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, irrigation, and mechanization.
 
• **MS Swaminathan** is considered the **father of the Green Revolution in India.**
 
• **Norman Borlaug** is known as the** 'Father of Green Revolution' in the world**.
 
• the **Government of India launched the Green Revolution in 1965** under the **Third Five-Year Plan(1961-66).**
 
• The Green Revolution within India led to an increase in agricultural production, especially in Haryana, Punjab, and Uttar Pradesh.
